subject: Whitestone POC: scope, success criteria, and integration next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Alex Greene <alex@whitestone.ai>
Cc: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 15 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Whitestone POC: scope, success criteria, and next steps

Alex — thanks again for the demo this morning. Quick recap from our side and a proposed POC plan so we can align on timelines and owners.

Call summary (30m):
- Goal: evaluate Redwood inference for low-latency document understanding pipeline (per-call latency < 150ms for 512 tokens; end-to-end integration with streaming for progressive results).
- Data: 500K anonymized documents; sample connector will pull from S3; we discussed residency in us-west.
- Stakeholders: Alex (ML), Priya (Product), Procurement team (contracts).

Proposed POC (4 weeks):
1) Week 0: Kickoff & access — API keys + sandbox dataset ingestion.
2) Week 1: SDK integration + streaming proof-of-concept (progressive partial results).
3) Week 2: Throughput tuning & batch/latency profiling; perf targets and cost estimates.
4) Week 3: Acceptance run and handoff to infra for production rollout.

Success criteria (needs your signoff):
- Latency: median generation latency <= 150ms for 512-token inference in our sandbox, p95 < 350ms.
- Accuracy: task-F1 within 3 points of your current baseline on the 1K eval set.
- Integration: streaming partial responses implemented; SDK routes using function/tool-calling for entity enrichment.
- Ownership: Redwood provides SDK + streaming route, Whitestone owns ingestion and eval harness.

Next steps (please reply with any changes):
- Alex/Priya: confirm success criteria and dataset availability by Tuesday (18 May).
- Procurement: will we need an MSA or a SOW for the trial?
- Redwood: attach POC template and a short SDK checklist (attached).

Attachments: whitestone-poc-template.pdf

Thanks,
Marissa
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Account Executive | Redwood Inference
From: Alex Greene <alex@whitestone.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Priya Reddy <priya.reddy@whitestone.ai>, Whitestone Procurement <procurement@whitestone.ai>, Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 15 May 2027 13:05:27 -0700
Subject: Re: Whitestone POC: scope, success criteria, and next steps

Marissa — appreciate the clear recap. A few clarifications from our side: 

1) Success criteria: the latency numbers look reasonable; for accuracy we'll share a 1K eval set (anonymized) — aim is within 3 points of our current model as you suggested.
2) Data residency: we need the trial environment to be hosted in us-west only (no replication outside region). Is that possible for a sandbox?
3) Streaming: important that partials include confidence metadata so our front-end can decide when to display intermediate results.
4) Procurement: we prefer a short trial SOW rather than a full MSA for the initial POC; procurement will draft a one-page SOW and loop in legal if needed.

I can confirm dataset availability by Monday EOD (17 May). Can Redwood share the streaming API route and any rate-limiting expectations so we can scope infra?

Thanks,
Alex Greene
Director of ML Systems | Whitestone AI
From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 15 May 2027 17:30:45 -0700
Subject: INTERNAL: Whitestone POC — technical ownership & implementation plan

Team — internal coordination after Alex's reply. Keeping this thread in Sofia's inbox for the external context. Action items and owner assignments below.

Implementation plan (detailed):
- Sandbox environment: Sofia to request a dedicated us-west sandbox (no cross-region replication). Owner: sofia_ivanova.
- SDK + Streaming: Ben to lead SDK samples, provide Node/Python streaming snippets and function-calling examples for entity enrichment. Deliverable: redwood-sdk-streaming-snippets.zip. Owner: ben_carter.
- Routing & Rate limits: Karthik to draft recommended routing policy (canary to hosted model, fallback to lower-cost quantized variant) and expected rate-limit thresholds for the POC (500 rps burst, sustained 150 rps). Owner: karthik_iyer.
- Eval harness: Marissa to coordinate the 1K eval label set from Whitestone and define the pass/fail criteria around F1. Owner: marissa_cole.

Integration notes to include in the external-facing doc:
- API route: POST /v1/streams/generate with chunked-transfer encoding (streaming partials).
- Tool calling: use structured function schema in the request; Redwood will return "tool_call" tokens interleaved with text chunks.
- Auth: short-lived sandbox keys; rotate per week.

I attached an internal SDK checklist to make sure we cover edge cases during the POC. I'll create a brief runbook for the us-west sandbox provisioning.

Attachments: sdk-integration-checklist.md

Sofia Ivanova
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Alex Greene <alex@whitestone.ai>
Cc: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 16 May 2027 10:20:12 -0700
Subject: Technical notes + streaming snippets for Whitestone POC

Alex — attaching a small bundle with streaming examples and a README that shows the recommended API routes and best-practice parameters for low-latency inference. Highlights below: 

- Recommended route: POST https://api.redwood.com/v1/streams/generate
  - headers: Authorization: Bearer <sandbox-key>
  - use chunked transfer; each chunk should include: {"type":"input_chunk","seq":n} and server returns partials as {"type":"partial","chunk_id":n,"confidence":0.83,...}
- Function/tool-calling: include a functions[] schema; Redwood will emit a single tool_call event per relevant token window.
- Batching: for best p95 latency, set batch_size=1 and enable prefix caching for repeated contexts.
- Rate limiting: sandbox policy will allow 150rps sustained, 500rps burst — we can raise for short windows if needed.

See attached: redwood-sdk-streaming-snippets.zip (contains node_stream_example.js, python_stream_example.py, README.md).

On a separate note: Sofia — I'll add a short snippet that shows injecting confidence metadata and a sample client-side rule to surface partials only when confidence > 0.6.

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
